insight.title: Spider Webs Sacrifice Tiny Sections to Survive Storms
insight.subtitle: By allowing individual threads to snap under extreme pressure, a web protects its entire structure from collapsing.
insight.notificationHook: How spider webs use controlled damage

sections.text: During a violent storm, a spider web does not fight the wind. Instead, it allows extreme local forces to break individual threads while the rest of the structure remains perfectly intact and standing.

Spider silk possesses a unique molecular structure. Under light pressure, it remains elastic. But under severe stress, the targeted thread softens, absorbs the impact energy, and snaps cleanly before transferring tension outward.
This localized sacrifice prevents a chain reaction. Instead of the entire web collapsing under a heavy blow, the spider only needs to repair a single, easily replaceable thread.
Engineered to break, so the whole may survive.
